original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: D-local H1 relaxation (PR1306 model): certify equal restricted/unrestricted minimum unit XOR counts of the fully restored dirty shear for every binary K of shapes 2x4, 2x5, 2x6 and 3x5; prove the uniform H=1/T=1 weight lemma and the H x T / T x H duality; together with PR1306, PR1557 and PR1706 this closes every shape with H+T <= 8.
scope_change_reason: PR1194/PR1311 cover the card's original H2/K question; PR1306 isolated the retained D-local feedback restriction and PR1557/PR1706 extended it. This answers PR1706's stated next question (certify the remaining shapes up to eight registers).
bottleneck_link: A strictly cheaper feedback prefix would be a legal D-local scalar saving under PR1306's substitution lemma; this closes that possibility for every prefix with at most eight registers. Side result for the bit supplier (the bit side does not bind); no kappa claim.
stop_rule: Stop once the four shapes are certified with witnesses and an independent check, and the lemma and duality are proved and numerically controlled; do not attempt nine registers.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json: 2x4 (256 K, max 6), 2x5 (1,024, max 7), 2x6 (4,096, max 8), 3x5 (32,768, max 10), 296 orbits with replayed restricted witnesses, zero feedback gains; lemma checked on 1x4..1x6 and 4x1..6x1, duality on 2x5/5x2, PR1306 3x3 reproduced; code-disjoint column-packed independent check of all 38,144 labeled K.
author: rtyu193-rgb
ai_assistance: Claude Code (Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5) wrote both checkers, the proofs and the prose; one session, no subagents, no independent human review.

open_questions.question: Does feedback ever save gates at nine registers (2x7, 3x6, 4x5), or is there a general no-feedback theorem (geodesic convexity of the block-lower-triangular subgroup of GL(H+T,2) for unit transvections)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A general theorem closes the D-local feedback relaxation for every prefix size; a counterexample would be the first legal cheaper prefix to price physically.
open_questions.first_step: Certify 2x7 with matrices packed in two 64-bit words and a radius-5 census (its expected maximum fits the ten-gate horizon).
open_questions.blocked_by: 3x6 and 4x5 need radius-6 unrestricted balls or a new reduction; no proof beyond the one-helper/one-target lemma is known.
